title: Disaster scams & false aid offers
label: FRAUD & DOCUMENTS
deck: Pause before paying, sharing identification or following an urgent aid message. Verify the organisation using a contact you find independently, ask for written terms and avoid pressure to pay immediately. Keep emergency funds for verified essentials. A logo, uniform or forwarded link does not establish trust.

Share only what the verified process needs. Never give account passwords, one-time codes or a full identity document to an unverified caller.
Unexpected upfront fees, gift cards, cryptocurrency or pressure to pay immediately are warning signs. Ask for written terms and time to review.
Verify relevant credentials, references and a written scope before hiring. Do not let a door-to-door offer rush you into unsafe entry or a large advance payment.
Keep receipts and message details without engaging further. Use verified consumer-protection or legal support when safe and available.

decisions: First decision: Find an independent contact

Use the organisation’s known website or an existing trusted number rather than the contact in an unsolicited message. Confirm the specific programme or provider. Decide which person can carry this out immediately and what would prevent it in your current location. Do not delay the protective step to complete a household worksheet.

If reporting channels are unavailable, stop contact, protect remaining money and accounts, and retain the records for later. A promised refund is not a reason to make another payment. Reassess the next available location or resource using the warning signs in this guide; do not assume a promised service is operating.

An offer of transport or shelter may also carry exploitation risk. Do not surrender documents or separate from family because a stranger promises priority assistance. Check the actual route and the needs of the person who will have the most difficulty moving. A destination is not confirmed until access and conditions have been checked.
